chat.title: Chat with Hamza
chat.subtitle: Talk it through first — ideas, plans, questions. Work starts only when you say so.
chat.empty: No messages yet. Say hello to Hamza — he runs the company for you.
chat.placeholder: Write to Hamza — (Enter sends, Shift+Enter = new line)
chat.planModeHint: Hamza drafts a plan with you — nothing is executed.

overview.what: Your executive summary. One glance: what the company is doing right now, what waits for you, and how money moves.

sections.b: Live counters: work running or queued, items waiting for your approval, today's cost, and the size of the AI workforce. Each card counts real records at the moment the page opens.
The company's heartbeat: work in motion right now, the newest activity, and whether any spending brake has been pulled.
Every number is counted live from the company's own work and spending records. Nothing is typed in by hand, so there is nothing here to clean or reset.

chat.what: Your direct line to Hamza, the orchestrator who runs the company. Talk, plan, ask — nothing is executed until you press 'Send as a task'.

sections.b: Write to Hamza as you would to a general manager: ask, plan, think out loud. Talking never starts work by itself.
When a thought is ripe, one press hands it to the company as real work. Only then do employees start.
With plan mode on, Hamza first lays out a plan and waits for your yes before anything moves.
The conversation is stored in the company's own records, so Hamza remembers earlier context between visits.

live.what: Every movement of company work, the moment it happens. Each row is one piece of work; click it to see its full story.

sections.b: Each row is one movement: work taken, running, finished. The steps of the same piece of work fold into a single line so the list stays readable.
Click a row and its full story opens right below it: what was asked, who worked on it, how it ended.
Straight from the live work records, written by employees as they act. The records themselves are managed on the Tasks page, where rows can be selected and removed with an audit note.

intelligence.what: Signals worth your attention, picked from everything the company produced.

sections.b: Overnight work, approval load and cost of the last 24 hours: what happened while you were away, condensed.
The warnings most worth your eye right now; the full list lives on the Alerts page.
The newest recorded reasoning: why the system chose what it chose.
The last movements of live work, so you can judge the tempo without leaving this page.
Everything here is picked automatically from live runs, alerts and decision records. Nothing is written by hand.

approvals.what: Work that finished and waits for YOUR yes or no before it ships. Only outward-facing things stop here.

sections.b: Only work that faces the outside world stops here: money leaving, contracts, messages to anyone outside the company. Approve and it ships; reject and it stops.
Your past decisions, kept as history. Decided items can be selected and removed in bulk; the removal itself is recorded.
The bar above the list is always visible: select all, then approve, reject or remove many at once.
Rows are created by the company itself the moment a piece of work reaches the outward door. Nothing enters this list by hand.

alerts.what: Problems and warnings the company raised about itself.

sections.b: Each row is a problem or warning the company raised about its own work, with its seriousness level.
When the same work later succeeds, the old warning closes by itself. You can also select rows and remove them; removals are written into the audit diary.
Raised automatically by the working system, never typed in.

voice.what: The spoken line: ask a question by voice, the company answers by voice. Same rules as chat — asking is free, outward actions still need approval.

sections.b: Hold the button, speak, release: your words go to Hamza and the answer comes back out loud. Asking costs nothing and starts no work.
Every finished call with its topic in a few words. Select rows to remove old calls; removals are recorded.
Each call is stored in the company records with what was heard and what was answered.

org.what: The whole holding at a glance: companies, departments, and who leads what.

sections.b: Companies at the top, departments under them, people under those. Click any person to see their role, manager and which AI brain they run on.
Drawn live from the employment records; it changes the moment the workforce changes.

companies.what: The companies inside the holding. Each one runs on the same operating system.

sections.b: How many companies, departments and employees the holding has in total.
Each card is one company: its departments, headcount and cost over the last 7 days.
When the holding spawns a sub-company, it registers here as a real row and runs on the same operating system.
The live company and employment records, plus the spending ledger for the cost figures.

departments.what: All departments with their directors and team sizes.

sections.b: Departments, how many are active, total staff, and 7-day cost across all of them.
Every department with its team size and what it cost today and over the last 7 days.
The live employment records and the spending ledger; the table mirrors them at every visit.

directors.what: The department heads — each one manages their team autonomously and reports upward.

sections.b: How many directors there are, how many have their character sheet and discipline hook attached, and how many departments are led.

Each department head, the department they lead, the AI brain they run on, and how much freedom they act with. 'Persona' is the written character and duties of the employee; 'bound' means it is attached and enforced.
The live employment records, same source as the Employees page.

employees.what: Every employee in the company, their role and current status.

sections.b: The whole workforce, how many are active, how many are dormant, and how many departments have active staff.
Everyone employed: role, department, AI brain and status. Filter by department above; only active staff do work.
The live employment records. Archived people remain as history — they never work and never appear as active.

hr.what: Hiring, probation and performance for the whole workforce.

sections.b: The people who run hiring and performance — themselves employees of the company.
The 7 things every new hire must have before starting (character sheet, duties, access and the rest), checked automatically.
Headcount and status per department.
New hires still being watched before they earn full status.
HR runs its checks automatically every night and writes the results into the employment records this page reads.

projects.what: The company's projects with their goals, risks and progress.

sections.b: Each card is one project: its goal, progress and open risks. Click a card to open the project's full page.
Kept up to date by the working teams; risk rows join in from the company risk register.

revenue.what: Where money comes from: income streams and their health, from real revenue records only — nothing simulated.

sections.b: The measurable income goals the company signed up to, with live progress.
One number summarizing the lasting value the company is building: income quality, cost discipline and risk, weighed together.
Openings that could become income, staged from first spotted to won.
Real income and pipeline records only. Nothing here is projected or simulated.

portfolio.what: Revenue portfolios — the money-making ventures the company is running.

sections.b: Each row is one money-making venture: what it is, its state, and how it is doing. Active and stopped ventures are listed separately.
The live portfolio records kept by the revenue teams.

crm.what: Clients, contacts, requests and deals — the commercial memory of the company.

sections.b: Clients, requests, contacts and deals. Each tab is a live table of the company's commercial world.
Some fields are yours to edit; fields owned by the working company are locked and marked so.
Written by the company as commercial work happens, and by you where fields are editable.

opportunities.what: Openings the company spotted that could become revenue.

sections.b: Columns are stages; cards move to the right as an opening ripens toward income. Review and scoring happen automatically.
The live pipeline records written by the revenue teams.

objectives.what: The revenue goals the company is steering toward, with measured progress.

sections.b: Each row is one signed income goal: the target, the measure, and live progress toward it.
Progress is measured from real revenue records, never estimated.

workflows.what: Repeatable multi-step processes the company can run on demand or on schedule.

sections.b: Each row is one repeatable process with its steps and its latest outcome. The company runs them on demand or on a schedule.
The live process records, including each run's result.

tasks.what: Every unit of work: who took it, what happened, how it ended. This is the raw work ledger behind the friendlier pages.

sections.b: Work currently active, running, queued, and failed in the last 24 hours.
Every unit of work ever taken: who claimed it, its state and its importance. The friendlier pages all summarize this ledger.
Select rows and remove them; the removal is written into the audit diary so nothing disappears silently.
This is the raw record itself, written by employees as they work.

automations.what: Jobs that run by themselves on a schedule — nightly checks, cleanups, reports.

sections.b: Jobs that run by themselves: nightly checks, cleanups, reports. Each row shows its rhythm and its last run.
Processes that start on a clock or when a specific event happens in the company.
The scheduler's own records — the same machinery that actually fires the jobs.

runtime.what: The engine room: is the resident worker alive, are queues moving. If something stalls, it shows here first.

sections.b: The always-on engine that carries work day and night. If it stalls, this page shows it first.
How the last day's work ended, as a share of each outcome.
The engine's most recent pieces of work, in their rawest form.
The engine's own heartbeat and run records.

models.what: The AI brains the company can use, their jobs and costs. Add a model with just a name and a key — routing does the rest.

sections.b: Every AI brain the company may use: what it is for, its state, and whether it has passed its exam before getting real work.
A name and a key are enough — plus a note if you wish. The key goes straight into the vault; routing decides the rest.
The latest picks of which brain got which work, with the reason in plain words.
The model catalog and the live run records.

orchestration.what: How work is routed to brains: which kind of task goes to which model, and what happens on failure.

sections.b: Which kind of work goes to which brain, laid out slot by slot.
Cheaper brains are tried where quality allows; when one fails or is unavailable, the work climbs to a stronger brain automatically.
The registered routing rules. Every change to them is recorded and visible.

memory.what: What the company remembers long-term and why. Writing is disciplined so memory never burns tokens silently.

sections.b: How many memories exist, how many are trusted, where they are stored, and when the last one was written.
Each row is one memory with its kind, trust tier and confidence. Quarantined memories are not used until verified.
Click a row to see where the memory came from, when it expires, and what replaced it.
Writing into memory is deliberately disciplined: only distilled, verified facts are stored, so memory stays small and never silently burns money re-reading noise.
The company's own memory stores, with the origin of every record shown in its detail.

knowledge.what: The company's studied knowledge — notes and cards produced from real study sessions.

sections.b: Studied notes and cards: research, reports, procedures, policies and training material. Each was produced in a real study session, not copied in blindly.
The company library records; every item shows its origin.

library.what: Everything the company has collected to work with: documents, links, media. Each item shows where it came from.

sections.b: Everything collected to work with: documents, links, media, skills and plugins. The kind column says what each item is.
Every item shows where it came from — who added it and when, including the items you provided yourself.
The live library records; usage and access counts come from the working company.

skills.what: Studied abilities the workforce can use. Each one was learned and verified before appearing here.

sections.b: Abilities the workforce has studied and can use. Each was learned and verified before appearing here; unstudied abilities do not enter.
A skill is enabled only for the departments that need it, never for everyone by default.
The library records, including each skill's study and verification trail.

plugins.what: Installed capability packs. Each is enabled only for the departments that need it.

sections.b: Installed capability packs that extend what employees can do.
A pack is enabled only for the departments that need it, never for everyone by default.
The library records, including each pack's grant list.

mcp.what: External tool servers the company can reach, with least-privilege access per department.

sections.b: Each server is a door to outside tools: browsing, files, services. Doors open per department, with the least access that suffices.
Which department may pass through which door, and how wide that door opens.
The registered access profiles; every widening of access is recorded.

audit.what: The unchangeable diary of everything that happened — every action, by whom, when. Nothing is ever deleted from here.

sections.b: Every action ever taken, by whom and when. This diary cannot be edited or deleted by anyone — including the system itself.
Open a record for the plain-language story first; the technical raw content stays folded below for specialists.
Written automatically at the moment each action happens. By design there is no delete here — that is what makes it trustworthy.

decisions.what: Why things happened: the recorded reasoning behind every automatic decision.

sections.b: Each row is one automatic decision with its recorded reasoning: why the system chose what it chose. Identical batch decisions fold into one row with a count.
Written by the system at the moment of each decision; records cannot be edited afterwards. You can select rows and remove them; every removal is written into the audit diary.

risks.what: Known risks and their current state. Re-measured at the end of every work wave.

sections.b: Open risks, how many of them are serious, how many were resolved, and the total ever registered.
Each known risk with its seriousness, state and project. Risks close with a measured note, never silently.
The project teams' own risk register, re-measured at the end of every work wave.

policies.what: The rules the company enforces on itself — quality gates, spending checks, safety rails.

sections.b: The rules that stop money, contracts and outside messages until you approve them.
The quality gate every employee's work passes through; rejections land on the Violations page with their reason.
The written rules of the company, kept in the library where every employee can read them.
The registered rule records; changes are audited.

permissions.what: Who may do what: access boundaries per department and per tool.

sections.b: Which department may use which library item: skill, plugin or document.
The width of each department's access to outside tool doors.
The live grant records; every change is audited.

security.what: Security posture: secrets handling, access rules, and anything that needs hardening.

sections.b: Recent times work was rejected by a safety or quality rule.
The most sensitive recorded actions of the week, surfaced for your eye.
The standing security picture: secrets kept in the vault, least-access rules, and what still needs hardening.
The audit diary and the registered security rules.

violations.what: Times an employee's work was rejected by a quality gate, with the reason. High counts mean retraining.

sections.b: Each row is one time an employee's work was rejected by the quality gate, with the reason in plain words. Repeated rejections signal retraining.
The discipline engine's own records, written at the moment of rejection.

pnl.what: Profit and loss: real income minus real costs. No projections — measured money only.

sections.b: Each day's real income minus real cost, side by side.
Which income engine earned what over the last month.
What published content earned, per platform.
The newest income records, most recent first.
Enter money that arrived. Incoming money needs no approval — only money leaving the company does.
The live income and spending ledgers. Measured money only; nothing projected.

costs.what: What running the company costs, by day and by source. Fed from the live spend ledger.

sections.b: Pick a period, department or model at the top; every panel below follows your choice.
The same spending cut four ways: by department, by model, by mode of work, and by day. Click a day to see that day's ledger.
The newest spending records, one row per piece of finished work.
The live spend ledger, written as each piece of work completes. These records are the company's permanent spending history.

tokens.what: AI usage by department, model and day. Filter above; everything below follows the filter.

sections.b: Pick a period, department or model at the top; every panel below follows your choice.
AI usage cut three ways: by model, by department, and by day — so you can see who uses what, and when.
Usage from building the company itself, kept separate so it never masquerades as company operations.
The live usage ledger, written as each piece of work completes.

budgets.what: Spending limits per department and how close each one is to its ceiling. Hard stops protect the monthly budget.

sections.b: Each department's spending ceiling and how close it stands. At 100%, non-critical work stops by itself.
The warnings fired as a ceiling nears (at 70%) or is hit.
The live spend ledger measured against the registered ceilings.

providers.what: The external AI providers behind the models, and how spend spreads across them.

sections.b: Each outside AI provider, the models riding on it, and how spending spreads across them.
The model catalog joined with the live spend ledger.

capacity.what: How much working capacity the company has and how much is in use.

sections.b: The rented server's muscle — memory and processing power — and how much of it is in use. The company runs on this machine day and night.
Live measurements taken from the machine itself.

settings.what: Company-wide switches, including the emergency pause that stops all work.

sections.b: Switches grouped by subject; pick a section on the left.
A switch can apply to the whole company, one department, or one employee — the narrower setting wins.
Risky switches are marked. Some changes stop for approval before applying; locked ones state why they are locked.
One switch stops all company work at once; releasing it lets work resume.
The company settings records; every change is audited.

integrations.what: Connected external services and their health.

sections.b: Every message meant for the outside world queues here and leaves only after approval.
The connection state of the commercial records: what writes into clients, requests, contacts and deals.
The services allowed to record income, each named in the ledger's source column.
Connections decided but not yet built, recorded openly instead of silently missing.
The live connection records and their own health checks.

health.what: Is every part of the system alive: database, queues, workers, voice.

sections.b: Whether each vital part is alive right now: database, queues, workers, voice line.
Open warnings grouped by seriousness.
The limits that decide when a warning fires; they follow the company settings.
The system checks itself continuously and writes what it finds; this page reads those checks.

logs.what: Raw system logs for deep troubleshooting.

sections.b: Audit entries, task events and decisions: the raw diaries behind every friendlier page.
All three streams only ever grow: new lines can be written, old lines can never be changed or deleted, by anyone.
Written directly by the working system. This page exists for deep troubleshooting.

backups.what: Copies of everything important, taken on schedule to the laptop and offsite storage.

sections.b: The core records are built so they cannot lose history even before any backup runs — old lines can never be changed.
Everything important is copied on schedule to the laptop and to offsite storage, so losing any single machine cannot hurt the company.
The backup jobs' own run records and the registered backup plan.
